label: <DEL> delimiter step
explanation: Fires on the <DEL> delimiter input at step t == L in every sequence (rate 1.0 at the delimiter), regardless of sequence length, original tokens, or digit count, with a near-constant magnitude (mean 1.31, median 1.32, max 1.45). It does not fire during the copy phase at all. In the original phase it fires only on about 134 of 3.2M steps, at very low magnitude (about 0.07 of max): the last original token of long sequences (L = 7-9), and these hold 0.0% of the activation mass. Magnitude varies only a little; the top examples are L = 6-7 sequences and the low-quartile samples are mostly L = 8-9, but I did not check this trend systematically.

issues: The main claim holds. On the test split, phase == 1 scores precision 1.0, recall 0.99975, F1 0.99988 and mass recall 0.99998. Every sequence fires at <DEL> and there are 0 false positives.
Profile figures match the explanation: mean 1.306, median 1.317, max 1.448; 0 of 2.73M copy-phase steps fire; 134 of 3.23M original-phase steps fire, holding 0.000 of the mass.

Minor inaccuracy: the stray original-phase activations are not just the 'last original token'. (phase==0)&(t==L-1) covers only 53 of the 134. All 134 have orig_idx >= 5, mostly orig_idx 6-7 (42 at 6, 87 at 7), i.e. the last or second-to-last token of L=7-9 sequences. Test misses show examples like 'y a t s h y [x:0.07] [r:0.07] <DEL>' (L=8, fires at positions 6 and 7). This is a tiny, ~0.07-of-max tail with 0% of the mass, so it does not affect the label.
Not verified: the claim that magnitude varies with L (top examples L=6-7, low quartile L=8-9). The explanation already says this was not checked systematically, and it is not load-bearing.
